question.text: Rebalancing frequency in a typical PMS strategy is:

answer.text: Time-based (monthly/quarterly/half-yearly/annual, with quarterly being popular) or threshold-based (e.g., 60% target with 50% and 70% trigger points)

explanation.text: The Logic: Time-based rebalancing can be done monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually, with quarterly being the popular choice. Threshold-based rebalancing uses upper and lower trigger points — for a 60% target weight, illustrative triggers are 50% and 70%. The Trap: "Never" leaves the portfolio drifting from policy weights; daily is excessive and not the cited norm; rebalancing only on cashflows misses standalone drift. Note: The 60% / 50% / 70% example is drawn directly from the cited source page.
